### Insteel Industries Reports Fourth Quarter 2026 Results


October 22, 2026


- [Download (opens in new window)](https://s21.q4cdn.com/425024259/files/doc_news/Insteel-Industries-Reports-Fourth-Quarter-2026-Results-2026.pdf)


MOUNT AIRY, N.C.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--


Insteel Industries Inc. (NYSE: IIIN) (“Insteel” or the “Company”), the largest manufacturer of steel wire reinforcing products for concrete construction applications in the United States, today announced financial results for its fourth quarter and fiscal year ended October 3, 2026.


**Fourth Quarter 2026 Highlights**


- Net earnings of $7.7 million, or $0.40 per share
- Net sales of $209.3 million
- Gross profit of $21.0 million, or 10.0% of net sales
- Net cash balance of $37.5 million and no debt outstanding as of October 3, 2026
- Announced the consolidation of welded wire operations
- Broader engineered structural mesh (“ESM”) customer base helped sustain shipments in a soft construction market
- Fiscal 2027 supported by a favorable demand outlook and ongoing operating efficiency initiatives


**Fourth Quarter 2026 Results**


Net earnings for the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026 decreased to $7.7 million, or $0.40 per share, from $14.6 million, or $0.74 per diluted share, for the same period a year ago. Results for the current quarter included $0.7 million in restructuring charges related to the consolidation of the Company’s welded wire operations, which reduced net earnings per share by $0.03.


Net sales increased 17.9% to $209.3 million from $177.4 million in the prior-year quarter, driven by higher average selling prices and increased shipments, which benefited from an extra week under Insteel’s fiscal calendar. Average selling prices rose 6.6%, reflecting pricing actions implemented in response to higher raw material, freight and other operating costs. Shipments increased 10.6%, largely due to the additional week, while a broader customer base within our engineered structural mesh business helped sustain volumes despite softness in the broader construction market. Sequentially, average selling prices rose 3.3%, while shipments increased 2.5% from the third quarter, also benefiting from the additional week.


Gross profit decreased to $21.0 million from $28.6 million in the prior-year quarter, with gross margin contracting to 10.0% from 16.1%. The year-over-year decline primarily reflected higher raw material costs, and inflationary trends affecting freight and operating costs that outpaced higher average selling prices.


Operating activities generated $18.2 million of cash during the quarter compared with using $17.0 million in the prior-year quarter, primarily due to favorable changes in net working capital, partially offset by lower earnings. Net working capital provided $4.6 million of cash in the current-year quarter compared with using $37.4 million in the prior-year quarter.


**Fiscal 2026 Results**


Net earnings for fiscal 2026 were $29.5 million, or $1.51 per diluted share, compared with $41.0 million, or $2.10 per diluted share, for fiscal 2025. Fiscal 2026 results included $0.8 million in restructuring charges, which reduced earnings per diluted share by $0.03. Fiscal 2025 results included $2.6 million of restructuring charges and acquisition-related costs, which reduced earnings per diluted share by $0.10.


Net sales increased to $739.5 million from $647.7 million for fiscal 2025, primarily driven by an 11.5% increase in average selling prices. Shipment volumes increased 2.4% from the prior year, benefiting from an additional week in fiscal 2026 under Insteel’s fiscal calendar and a broader customer base for the Company’s engineered structural mesh. Gross profit decreased to $75.7 million from $93.4 million in fiscal 2025, while gross margin declined to 10.2% from 14.4%. The reduction in profitability primarily reflected higher raw material costs and inflationary trends in freight and operating costs that outpaced higher average selling prices.


Operating activities generated $36.6 million of cash in fiscal 2026 compared with $27.2 million in the prior year, primarily due to favorable changes in net working capital, partially offset by lower net earnings. Net working capital used $12.8 million of cash in fiscal 2026 compared with $37.6 million in the prior year, largely reflecting a smaller increase in inventories.


**Capital Allocation and Liquidity**


Capital expenditures for fiscal 2026 increased to $11.8 million from $8.2 million in the prior year. For fiscal 2027, capital expenditures are expected to total approximately $30.0 million. Planned investments will primarily support expansion of the Company’s engineered structural mesh business, strategic investments in its prestressed concrete strand operations, cost reduction and productivity initiatives, and routine maintenance.


During the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026, the Company repurchased approximately 15,000 shares of its common stock under its existing share repurchase authorization, bringing total fiscal 2026 repurchases to approximately 114,000 shares. For the full year, Insteel returned $24.9 million to shareholders through dividends and share repurchases while maintaining a strong balance sheet and ample liquidity. The Company ended the year debt-free with $37.5 million in cash and cash equivalents and no borrowings outstanding under its $100.0 million revolving credit facility.


**Outlook**


“Our fourth quarter results reflect the challenging cost environment we have navigated for the last two years,” commented H.O. Woltz III, Insteel’s President and CEO. “Domestic wire rod prices remain at historically high levels, well above prices in global markets, while availability continues to be constrained, thereby requiring the Company to supplement domestic purchases with offshore purchases and accept the working capital implication of elevated import volumes. Higher freight costs and persistent inflation affecting most of our cost structure continue to challenge the Company. While we have recovered a substantial portion of elevated costs through price increases, rising costs are relentless. From a demand perspective, publicly funded infrastructure activity continues to provide a solid foundation for our business, while ongoing investment in data center projects constitutes the bulk of the activity we see in private nonresidential construction. Our pursuit of additional growth opportunities within our engineered structural mesh business has broadened our customer base and supported shipment growth. We expect this trend to continue throughout 2027.”


Woltz added, “As we enter fiscal 2027, we are focused on building on these growth opportunities while improving our cost competitiveness and operating efficiency. We are pleased with our progress expanding our engineered structural mesh business and with the previously announced consolidation of our welded wire operations, which we expect will result in substantial cost reductions. We will continue to invest in strategic initiatives that support long-term growth and have confidence that our balance sheet provides the flexibility to navigate changing market conditions and pursue additional opportunities.”


**Conference Call**


Insteel will hold a conference call at 10:00 a.m. ET today to discuss its fourth quarter and fiscal 2026 financial results. A live webcast of this call can be accessed on Insteel’s website at[https://investor.insteel.com](https://cts.businesswire.com/ct/CT?id=smartlink&url=https%3A%2F%2Finvestor.insteel.com&esheet=54626341&newsitemid=20261022365187&lan=en-US&anchor=https%3A%2F%2Finvestor.insteel.com&index=1&md5=e2f669d7ab7a5c15985f39be3d3c52d6) and will be archived for replay.


**About Insteel**


Insteel is the nation’s largest manufacturer of steel wire reinforcing products for concrete construction applications. Insteel manufactures and markets prestressed concrete strand and welded wire reinforcement, including ESM, concrete pipe reinforcement and standard welded wire reinforcement. Insteel’s products are sold primarily to manufacturers of concrete products and concrete contractors for use, primarily, in nonresidential construction applications. Headquartered in Mount Airy, North Carolina, Insteel operates 11 manufacturing facilities located in the United States.
